Up until now, I had never played an isometric RPG like this and I figured I'd add in my two cents for others like myself.  My previous experience has been with games like Skyrim, the Mass Effect series,  various shooters and an assortments of strategy games.  With that in mind, I was a little concerned that the pacing of this game would be an issue (having to pause repeatedly in combat, reading through a lot of text, the lack of flashy special effects and cutscenes, etc...).  Not only is it not an issue, I found that it was quite relaxing!  This game makes me want to play it while drinking a cup of hot tea while sitting in front of a crackling fire.  It's an experience to be taken slowly and savored.  I spent about 30 minutes in the character creation alone and loved all the various options that went into crafting the perfect hero.
I read some copmplaints here about the graphics quality, but it was a non-issue to me.  In fact, I have found that to be one of the things working in its favor.  In a weird way, not being bombarded with flashy special effects and cutscenes is one of the things that has helped make the game more immersive and relaxing to me.
I highly recommend this game.  It's deep, immersive and the story and world is charming and interesting.  It requires time and thought and is not a game that is designed to be rushed through, but I feel that it does a great job at rewarding the player's time investment.

If you ever wanted to play a JRPG but wanted real-time combat where you actually control a character instead of a menu, this is a good game to try. While the silent protagonist takes a bit out of the story, running around and hunting monsters is more than enough to make up for it.

This game tried to incorporate the many different styles of several distinguished RPG's and put it into one package. The result was not perfect, but MY GOODNESS did it strike close to the mark for what it is.
The leveling system will appeal to the hardcore stat-crunchers out there, but is organic enough to be learned by a more casual player as well. (THAT BEING SAID- I HIGHLY RECOMMEND LOOKING UP HOW THE LEVELING SYSTEM AND CLASS MECHANICS WORK. THANKFULLY THE GAME COMMUNITY HAS AN EXTENSIVE WIKI AND FORUM THREADS).
Its definitely a bit tough, but the game rewards being prepared ahead of time. It can also get a bit grindy, especially when doing notice board quests, however it will make you stronger and more prepared for potential difficulty spikes that occur later down the line. Again I cannot stress enough how effective the WIKI is, dont be afraid to look things up if needed. (especially regarding merchants and their respective idol quests.)

TL:DR Game mixes Blitz: The league and Mortal Kombat.
Soccer rage is a game that i found while browsing "Just good PC games" steam group, after clicking on it I was shown an interesting concept. You take the "no holds barred" aspect from Blitz: The League and mix with with equal parts FiFa 20XX and Mortal Kombat to make a smooth mixture when you can play dirty and really hurt your opponents.
Sold by this concept I bought the game and proceeded to download it, and that is unfortunately where the trouble began. Before I go further, I do want to point out that I am an American and really do not know the first thing about soccer...
While soccer really doesn't have a lack of violence, and violent overreactions. I would say (as an American) that it does lack a certain... Whats the word... Hyper violence that football possesses. Soccer Rage takes care of that in spades!
You are able to select one of eight teams (currently, more on the way). This does include Germany, England, Brazil, #murica, and Spain. So you can recreate grudge matches with the system (there is actually an achievement for that...). The avatars for the teams are interesting, possessing a semi-robotic/heavily armored chic with both home and away jerseys able to be selected. They are also unique enough in color choices that it is easy to see who is who while in the middle of a match.
The arena selection is slightly small, but they are really only just eye candy. The only difference besides visuals would be the music attached to them. As well as the occasional particle effect in the background.
Gameplay starts out with your team taking the field in 5, 7 or 11 man teams. Once kickoff starts (or whatever it is in soccer) it plays like normal fifa. Where you maneuver your men to steal a ball from the opponent and kick it into a goal. What makes this game different is the addition of 2 bars, a health and a rage bar. The health bar is fairly explanatory, the more you get hit, the less bar you have. Once you hit 0 health you explode. Let me restate this, THIS IS A SOCCER GAME WITH EXPLOSIONS. The second bar is the rage bar, this is gained through gameplay, stealing and getting stolen from, shooting a goal and so on. You can burn some of the rage bar to fuel extra special attacks. Whether it is a bugger of a kick, an exceptionally difficult pass, a brutal tackle, or an invitation to scrap.
When you do successfully start a scrap, the entire team surrounds the two, cheering and hooting much like a high school fight. There the gameplay changes drastically. The two fighters then have a limited time to lay as much smack down on the opponent as they can. This is a very VERY good way to drop an opponents health or to take him out of the match entirely.
To wrap this up, its a very enjoyable game to play! Admittedly it started out a little rough for win10 users, however the devs are nice people and worked very hard to set things right. Now i look forward to having some friends over and having a good couch multiplayer session with this game. Just to see what happens...

I bought this game even though I couldn't really find any videos nor reviews in English for it.
Seeing as there are still no reviews in English after I spent two hours on this game, I figured I'd write one!
Weapon Shop Fantasy is basically a management game where you hire "Staff" that craft and go on adventures for you. You gain materials by sending your Staff members on adventures, which you then use to craft equipment. Every crafting "table" uses a different stat. For example, the forge, where you make ingots, uses the Vitality stat. Vitality increases your character's melee defense stat. Using the Forge will increase you Strength, Crafting Table increases Dexterity, and Enchanting Table, Intelligence.
The higher your stats are on a Staff member, the better gear they will craft using these "tables", which means they'll be worth more money. There are several quests/objectives to complete. There seems to be two types I've encountered so far, static quests and timed quests. The timed quests give you a nice amount of money, while the static quests seem to always unlock new recipes.
With all that said, the game is quite grindy, at least in the beginning, because you need to constantly send your Staff on adventures to grab resources, then craft a few things, sell, and repeat. It takes a bit of time to progress through the game at first, but it seems to be taking off now that I'm getting higher stats (50+) on one of my adventurers, he comes back with a full inventory on most adventures.
Also, I believe this game is translated from Chinese and, quite frankly, there are a LOT of typos in there. I personally don't mind it, but there definitely is a lot of work to put into correcting all of them. And it's not just typos, there is a lot of information/speech that is simply not written properly, sentences that make no sense. You get a good idea of what the developpers mean, but it's really poorly written.
Besides that, I haven't encountered any bugs, and I've had fun with the game so far! I'm excited to see what the devs have planned for the future!

NOTE: This review is written while the game was in Early Access at 25th of april.
You know, I've always been a person who likes to build stuff. That's why I LOVED to play with LEGO. I used to build all kinds of stuff. Cars, buildings...whatever I preferred, as long as I knew how the pieces connected to eachother. Because how hard is it to build a tower when you don't know how your tools and bricks work? That would be a mighty challenge even for master builders...
The hobby of building things kind of continued when I started playing video games, so I bought a game like MyWorlds before called Fight the Dragon. That game had an amazing level editor with lots of tools to play with, including a lot of ''invisible'' mechanisms like triggers and such. Unfortunately that game is suffering a slow and silent death due to lack of players, which brought me back to the quest of finding a game where I could express my fountain of imagination.
Advertisements of FtD aside, because I often stick to a certain game and don't often buy new games myself, a friend of mine decided to bring me into this game by gifting it to me. I saw the game earlier on Steam and I didn't know if I would like it as much as the previous game mentioned, because it was early access and it played very differently. But since the game was gifted to me, I decided to give it a try.
So the game started freshly right into the hub. As my character opened his eyes, I could see a new and wonderful world to explore. It had an atmosphere of simplicity to it, which made me happy because I love to play a simple fantasy RPG where I dont have to think 24/7 so I can relief the stress I built up through the day, and it was also an indication that the level editor, which I will obviously abuse in the future, wouldn't be that complex, which I think is a huge bonus.
The game looks pretty simple, and I will be truly honest with you: it is. When I entered one of the default worlds, it became clear that the things you can do in a map were pretty limited. The quest and skills system are very cool already, but they're quite limited. At the moment there are only 2 kind of quests and 1 class (although there are some awesome outfits for it), which makes the game pretty basic in my opinion. At this moment the game clearly is in an early access state, where the game is playable and enjoyable, but just lacks features you would otherwise expect in a game of its genre. But as time goes on, the game will grow like our own children and hopefully make the world a better place when its standing on its own.
Although I might have sounded a bit negative about the game, I'm 100% in love with this game right now, because in my opinion some of the game's features, like the level editor, the details of the models and the combat system, are godly already and I can't wait to see more and more added to them. I really see some good potential in this game and I'm sure this game will claim a special spot in my heart, just like FtD. But for that it needs a little bit more content to feel complete, like puzzles, dungeons and just expansions of the already existing features.
So long story short: At this day, the game is truly in ''Early Access''. I really like to play it. I love the atmosphere and how the game works, but it might feel a bit incomplete after playing for a while. I do recommend the game when you just love level editors because MyWorld's editor is a beast. And if you like simple RPGs, I would definitely throw advertisements of this game in your face for days. Otherwise I would recommend to wait with buying and reconsider it, especially if you already have high expectations for Action RPGs because you played the heck out of The Witcher 3 or Dark Souls. This game (as is) just isn't like Dark Souls. It has its own unique aspects (like its simplicity and level editor) which make it stand out from those games. So please don't dislike the game because it's not like any of them.
Personal Score: 7.5/10

NOTE: This game was given to me by the developer for review purposes. This did not influence my review in any way.
Note: MyWorld - Action RPG Maker is currently in Early Access. The version reviewed was current as of the date of this review.
MyWorld - Action RPG Maker (from here on, just "MyWorld" for brevity) is a 'light' action RPG mixed with a 'light' action RPG development tool; or at least that's the best I can come up with to describe it. It's developed by The Game Creators -- the same development company that created App Game Kit and Game Guru -- both game development toolkits available on Steam.
Graphics - The graphics in MyWorld mostly look like something taken from quite a few years ago, such as a late PSX or early PS2 game. There are a few differences, such as greater draw distances and some special effects and dynamic lighting, but the 'game' takes a basic, low-poly approach to graphics. This ensures that it runs well, but it doesn't look that great even next to other games that take a similar approach, such as the recent For the King. Characters, in particular, look blocky and unattractive.
The interface is minimal, but also not that useful. There are no tooltips; mouse mode (press 'm') gives you a mouse pointer, but doesn't stop mouse movements from also rotating the camera; and the little help menu in the bottom right looks like it was tacked on as an afterthought. It may just be an Early Access placeholder, though, so I'm not too worried about it at this point in time.
There are some simple graphics settings, including draw distance and a detail slider, as well as screen resolution. Even with 'Ultimate' graphics in 1920x1080, though, the game doesn't look that good. At least it runs well, though.
Sound - There are no voices and no music. Sound effects are minimal, although the bird sound track is quite nice. Again, I assume there will be more sound assets added as the game progresses through Early Access.
Gameplay - MyWorld has two components to it: the game and the world creator.
The game part plays like a very basic third-person action RPG. You move with WASD and swing your weapon with one of the mouse buttons. You can also roll and use four relatively basic abilities, each of which has a different cooldown period. They're not really explained, but they're easy to understand once you try using them in combat. There are very basic NPC interactions available, including simple quests of the go, collect, or kill variety.
Combat itself is very basic, and very clunky. It feels like a few disconnected animations chained together in ways that don't really work very well, and is not satisfying in the least. If you've played basically any other third-person action RPG in the last 15 years, you'll be disappointed by the current state of the combat in MyWorld. I can only hope it will get much better before the game leaves EA, as it's really the core of the game part of the product.
When you create a new world, you first start out in game mode on an empty expanse of terrain. Pressing ESC takes you to creation mode, where you can build your (rather limited at present) work of art. The interface here also has no tooltips or explanations, but it's mostly easy to use, and there are some in-game videos if you really need them.
The creation palette includes terrain modification, choice of a few different environments or themes, and placement of pre-fabricated objects, or props. The store page mentions "over 200 props", but really it's not very many; certainly not enough to avoid most worlds looking the same as most others. And the props are almost all static: they don't actually do anything, other than break (uselessly) when you hit them with your sword.
I was momentarily excited when I saw a section of a guide video about creating props, but it turns out it was my misunderstanding. There is no way currently to create props, NPCs, environments, or basically anything else. You're restricted to terrain deformation, placement of pre-fabricated assets, and some extremely limited quest creation. Again, I'm hopeful that there's a lot more coming.
Other than the combat-oriented worlds and the world creation tool, the game also has "Hub World", which is where you start each time you load up the game. This provides portals to the pre-created worlds, your own created worlds, and the Steam Workshop for the game, where you can try out other users' created worlds. You can also change your character model to one of four presets.
Pros:
+ It's a nice idea
+ Dynamic lighting is good
+ Terrain deformation in the world creator is quite nice
Cons:
- Combat is clunky and not fun
- World creation tool is very limited
- Graphics are disappointing
I'd like to recommend MyWorld, but at this point I don't think I can do so in good faith. As a game, it's not much fun. And as a development tool, it's too basic to make anything that's any more fun. I really hope the developers make it a better game and provide a lot more tools for those who want to create worlds, but as it is right now, it's not that great at either.

A nostalgic romp in an original and engaging world. Obsidian has made good on it's promise to bring you a fantastic and unforgiving isometric RPG.
If you've played games like Baldurs Gate, or Planescape: Torment, then you know what you're getting into, but for the uninitiated, this is a text heavy roleplaying game. Instead of the constant grinding of enemies to level up associated with most similar games currently on the market, your experience will largely be rewarded from exploring new areas and completing quests, of which you'll find plenty.
This is not to say that the combat system was neglected, it is both engaging and relentless. You'll need to take control of your entire party (unless you choose to go solo) and plan your attacks and formations accordingly. A host of spells, abilities and talents help you maintain control of the battlefield in real time as you dispatch your foes and progress through an compelling and well written story. Definitely a contender for Game of the Year.

I think the community puts too much of an emphisis on the difficulty of this game, It's not that hard, you just need to know what your doing.
First off, they put a lot of work into this games lore, they really know how to build the world and make it feel real. (You do need to go looking for it though, read item descriptions)
The voice acting is iffy for some characters, and absolutly increadible for even more
The combat is amazing, it teaches you to balance dodges, blocks, parries, attacks, kicks, and healing. I've gotten sick of games where you just have to walk up to an enemy and press buttons to win. Dark Souls: Prepare to Die is a game of skill, not luck.
If you have friends who play this game, don't listen to them most of the time. A friend of mine told me I'd have such a hard time fighting the "Four Kings," and I beat it on my first try. The game is about intimidation, and it does a very good job at it, just use your brain to guide your hands, not your hands and nothing more.
There are several moments in the game where it becomes outrageously unfair, but the rest of the game outweighs such parts
You will die many, many times, but a lot of deaths does not point to impossibility or unfairness
This is a very polished game, and I recomend it to you 100%

I got this game a few years ago. Back then it was still in beta, and while it had a fair amount of content, the story was lacking, the building felt empy, your ships were static, there were severe performance issues, and the balancing of weapons and abilities needed a lot of work.
I played it for a while, then set it down, because it was fun, but had limited merit.
When 1.0 came out recently, I decided to pick it up again and see what had changed.
Wow!
They really improved it. The game has a reasonably compelling story now, it has endless quests that are actually well implemented, you can build new villages, recruit new settlers, recruit more crew members to your ship and upgrade your ships from dinky boxes to hulking behemoths.
They've rebalanced things a lot, added more content, made farming awesome, and just created enough richness that you can enjoy the game for hundreds of hours.
When you've got max level gear, you can stomp the easy enemies, but you can still get killed by the strongest ones if you're reckless. The bosses are all dynamic and fun to fight, and this missions they added to get to them are frankly kind of awesome.
They've improved the richness of the cultures, even though they did have to remove a few things that didn't fit with the improved lore.
There are still things they could do to build upon the game and make it even better, but it's a fully functional version with a lot of cool features.
Some people compare the game to Terraria. I've played both, and here's what I'll say. Terraria's progression system is longer, there are a lot more steps, a lot more boss fights, and while you're doing that, Terraria might be more intense. However, once you've beaten the bosses a few times and maxed out your gear in Terraria, things just feel kind of empty. There's not enough end game content to keep you entertained for that long.
Starbound is different. There are a lot more biomes, sub-biomes, places to explore, and total content. Starbound has dozens of times the number of building items, and trillions of times the landmass to explore. There are so many cool little things that you'll discover on adventures that will make you smile, and the capacity to have pets, and to build new villages has really given you a reason to build cool places.
The developers have done a great job with this, and I hope they add even more cool things in the future. For $15, this is a great deal. Happy travels to you.

It's like the 1990-2000s of the role-playing gaming finally returned and not like trendy HD re-issues of the old RPGs, but as a true spiritual successors! Pillars of Eternity looks and feels like Baldurs Gate with a modern graphics while the old athmosphere of the vast world full of adventures remains there fully. The main plot seems intriguing and well-written, while the sub-quest are quite fun too and often offer moral dilemmas that are not easy to solve. Most of the people I know who play CRPGs consider the Infinity Engine games like Baldur's Gate I & II, Icewind Dale, Planescape Torment, Fallout 1 & 2 (although they were not IE) to be the "Golden Age" of RPGs. It's been sort of downhill since. Oblivion & Skyrim were beautiful but sort of empty and in my opinion unplayable without mods. And many of the RPGs of the last 10 years forgot the RP part. Yes I'm talking about you Fallout 3, Dungeon Siege, etc.
Well, RPG fans, if you loved and missed Baldur's Gate & Icewind Dale, you will LOVE Pillars of Eternity. It is everything that was good about them come again with a modern look and feel. The level of detail, atmosphere, design craft, and forethought that went into this game is amazing. It is beautiful to look at, interesting to play with compelling characters and deep dialouge trees that really let you role play and tease the details of the story out.
The game play is not perfect. And for those not used to the IE style of play might have some trouble getting used to it at first, but you will quickly master it. This is not Dragon Age, they won't ram the plot down your throat you have to work for it. Talk to people. It is not an Elder Scrolls game with unlimited exploration over a world that turns out to be sort of empty and after a while all looks the same. Each area in PoE is smaller but alive with activity.
Give this a try. If you've never played the old IE games after this you'll want to. If you have and loved them, this is the game you have been waiting for for years.

I heard about this game in 2012. Now it is finally released.
PoE is a trip down the memory lane. I am an old guy and have been waiting 15 years for something like this to happen.
I am a big rpg fan, have been playing tabletop and lots of crpg's.
So should you get this game. Did you ever play Baldur's Gate? Did you like it? Then get this!!
Obsidian pitched this game as a spiritual successor of the old IE games (Baldur's Gate) and it is. The rules are different, as this is NOT D&D. But the feel, the mood, the sound and even the graphics (though very updated, it's been 15 years) reminds me so much of the good old days.
That beeing said the game is not flawless. But I have been playing 15 hours with no major bugs.
There are many small bugs though, but compared to other releases. it is running quite smooth... Even on my old machine (but I do have problems on the big maps, and with loading screen time)
If I should warn ppl about anything, it would be the differences from the old IE games. Yes there are many.
The things that I personally find a little strange:
*The game is build with Unity, I would have preferred Obsidians own engine. Unity have ALOT of performance issues...
*No ammunition. I miss this from IE.
*Can't costumize your char in-game. Very bad. Not even change the portrait or voice!! (fixed in patch1.05)
*Stash (like your bag of holding) can't be sorted... (also fixed)
*Some npc's that join you are REALLY weak
*False options in dialogue.
*Un-necessary hand-holding
*Most chars you can build, are perhaps too similair. I have to play more, though
I am waiting for Obsidian to release their first patch, and that will hopefully take care of most of the problems. It is certainly their best release ever ...
ADDED: So, now that I've played through this, I must also warn about a mediacroe story, and this is not very replayable... There is still some issues with UNITY, that engine is really hard on your CPU, and I guess I am dissappointed in the minimum specs, that kept going up, my PC was brandnew when I bought this (pre) and I can hardly make it run smooth...

This game is bloody amazing. I have played it several times through on xbox 360 and twice on PS3. I had to buy it on PC to get the feel for it and in all honesty, it is a million times better on PC than console. I go by several factors when reviewing games.
Firstly graphics: I always ask myself how the games surroundings make me feel. Do they suck me into a new world or not? Is it breath taking? Can the PC/console keep up with the graphics itself? My answer to this is yes. On the PC the graphics are amazing, they suck me right into the game and the PC can keep up with the rate needed to not lag whilst trying to load up scenary.
Second I look at the main protaganist: Commander Shepard, (I am playing Fem Shep) is a character you can make your own. You can choose the background of Shep, his/her personality and the kind of hero you wish to be. I enjoy the fact that she has varied emotion though sometimes it doesn't sound like she does. All in all Shep is a decent protaganist to play.
Thirdly I look at the story itself: The story in ME1 is the beginning of something beautiful. You can just feel it when you start to play. I have spent 17 hours just doing side missions, (I am a completionist like that and some side missions are only available for a limited time) I am about a third through the main story campaign and through side missions and planet searching I am a level 27. The main story for me is amazing. It threads together beautifully and it continues through ME2 and 3. Some parts of the story got to me and some really annoyed me. All in all an amazingly well made story line!
Next I look at handling of the character: Movement in a character is important for me. I hate feeling like the controls are stiff or that my character isn't moving well. Shep moves quite easily. My problem is the MAKO. The vehicle. It handles like a trolley on a skateboard with two wheels missing. It is dodgy, I constantly kept dying in the MAKO because I couldn't turn it properly. It isn't so bad when landing on a planet to do a side mission or search for precious metals etc, it sucks more on the missions where you are required to use a MAKO. For example: I used one on Feros to go to the ExoGeni lab and I died several times before I ended up plowing through the enemies. A word of advice would be to take it slowly whilst using the MAKO.
Next I look at allies: The people who you fight with are the most important of all. I need to know those AI will help me in a tough fight. You get six allies to choose from, two of which you can take out on each missions. Mix it up to find your perfect allies. You get;
Ashley Williams: You meet her on the first mission and she ends up joining your team. A stable fighter.
Kaiden Alenko: A L2 Biotic with a lot of force and power in biotics. (I use Kaiden a lot for throw and barriers)
Garrus Vakarian: A Turian with a tough can do attitude. This guy is pure military fighter. Handy if you like to kick some butt.
Urdnot Wrex: A Krogan with the same attitudes as Garrus but tougher and very grumpy.
Tali'Zorah nar Rayya: A Quarian on her own adventure, she is useful for hacking and decrypting. (I use Tali every time)
Liara T'soni: An Asari who is very useful in the field of biotics.
Lastly I look at enemies: The main enemy in ME1 is the Geth. You find other enemies on the way but you will mainly find Geth. Not to hard to kill and easy enough to run away from if needed. They are a well thought out enemy with a good back story. Enjoy that!!
To summarise my really long review, this game is amazing and I recommend it to every single person ever!!

Pros

* Great visuals/audio and environment.
* Great storyline and progression.
* Excellent soundtrack that did not annoy even throughout the entire play through

I have many gripes. This game smells like it was a magnum opus from the word go. A bit of constructive critism then.
Needs Fixing:
-Combat needs to be fluid and the gooie sticky feeling of the melee needs to be fixed.
-Leveling up needs to have weight rather than just being token, I feel it could be used to gain the abilities rather than them being unlocked from the get go.
-The hub world should be optional, if not removed. It puts a barrier between the player and the game. However, if you incorporated it into gameplay it wouldn't be a pain. Simply lessing the distances between things, removing some of the clutter, scaling things back. That sort of thing. I can see it working better on an island or inside a house, but right now if feels like a rip from Runescape.
-A day night cycle perhaps?
-Making friendly NPC's can't be that hard eh lads? Just change their enemy flag to another team and make it an enemy to the originals with a reskin? No?
-Using the 'E' key as an action key and putting the potions anywhere else is desired. If popular culture dictates certain trends, it might be because they work well, such a thing is usually a good idea to follow.
-List the keys in a long page instead of bit by bit, its hard to navigate.
-The editing tools need a remake, more select and then click rather than click and boom there it is.
-Make the rotation not a single key, roundabouting is outdated and bad. Use the 'E and Q' keys, or the arrows.
-Enemy noises could be backed down a little, more boney, less gobliny, although I understand the artistic choice you took, so not too hard on it.
-Damage feedback is a bit wanky, sometimes an enemy will connect, sometimes it will not. It just depends on how the stars are I guess.
-Remove the videos from the hub world and add them in a tutorial section in a menu. (Escape is always menu, escape is always menu, escape is always menu, ect ect.)
-Blocking is needed. Dark souls works in dark souls because it blends both. This has only dodge rolling, and to a weird key. Why not have it as block + Run? Wait, no block.
-Health potions shouldn't be unlimited, every levelup I had I got new potions, which I used to kill enemies to get more potions. It takes alot of fun out of it.
-Do the NPC's have bricks on their shoes? Move them around, reskin a chicken or something please.
-"Alot of items, without need, is nothing." 200+ Objects is alot, yes. Ask for community suggestions. Add as many as you can that apply to more than one situation. I can only fight skeletons for so long you see. Let me farm something, anything.
-RPG Role playing game. This is actually more of an 3rd Person action game actually. It lacks alot of the critera to be classified as an RPG.
-Mayhaps add grass, flowers, rocks that are created on terrain? "It is dull to see a sea of green, without the creed of seed."

=-=-=-=-=
TL;DR
=-=-=-=-=
• Single Player only, no Co-Op or Multi-player mode, still a great 1-player game
• Good gfx, lighting and atmosphere. Spooky when looting houses
• Play stealthy or reckless; Smash zombies with Car Doors!!
• Addictive: I spent 12 hours with the game on first day of purchase!
• Google x360ce if you want to use a controller other than the x360 controller. You'll be glad you did.
=-=-=-=-=-=-=
So addictive, State of Decay will keep you hooked if you are into stealthy survival, gathering goods, managing a community, zombie combat/survival-horror or just about anything else this game offers.
Play with reckless abandon, charing into the fray with your Guns or Melee weapons, to achieve your goals, or stealthily sneak around the walking dead to search houses for food, water, ammo, building materials or other people for a greater chance of survival.
My favorite things about this game are the gathering aspects, the building of the base-camp, building a community with NPCs and managing Food, Medicine, Building materials, Ammo and vehicles.
My number one favorite thing about this game, in terms of play-mechanics, is quite simply; The awesome option of smashing zombies with your car door as you go careening by (or repeatedly slamming your car door into a zombie who fell over).
The biggest and most obvious gripe about this game, is the complete lack of any co-op or multiplayer modes. This game is wonderful as it is, but it would be amazing as an MMO or at least LAN Co-Op.
*** This Game is NOT Co-Op or Multiplayer: SIngle Player ONLY. ***
Thankfully, the developer, Undead Labs, has another game in the works (currently known as Class 4) based around the ideas of State of Decay. State of Decay can even be viewed as a testing game for their Online version of State of Decay/MMO Survival horror.
The graphics, spooky lighting and atmosphere are all in line with a game of this type and are done well. Many times I found myself turning off the flashlight becasue it kept attracting Zombies, so searching through abandoned houses for supplies in the dark (while hearing zombie moans ...somewhere close by) is a pretty creepy feeling and really adds to the suspense of the game.
The audio sounds a bit quiet, on my rig anyways. I have to turn my speakers up a bit to hear the game at better sound levels, even with the audio sliders at max in the settings. As long as you don't expect any other sounds from your system while playing this game, it works just fine. If you get a message from a friend on steam (or other service) while creeping around a house being stealthy, with the audio up to hear this game, expect to jump in your seat!
Overall, this game is really enjoyable to me. Open world Survival-horror with many RPG-style elements, building of communnities/outposts and NPC interactions just really help this game along. Again, it's not multi-player, but its a damn good game, in my opinion.

This review is coming from a returning player for the third time. I have already played and enjoyed this game on Xbox 360 and PS3 ports. This game is by far one of Capcoms best IPs they came out with yet really overlooked since it came out around the time of Kingdoms of Amalur and Dark Souls but this year coming to PC finally. This game is practically everything you would want in an action combat rpg with nice music, epic combat, fun monster fights, and funny moments.
~Pros~
-Best combat system made in a game feeling like a mix of Monster Hunter and Shadow of the Colosus with fighting monsters and even climbing ontop of them in a dark atmosphere that feels like you are in the world of a dark fantasy like dark souls.
-9 Classes to choose from being three standard, three advanced, and three hybrid classes each with their own playstyles with advantages and weaknesses as well as stat gain for your character so you can make the type of fighter you want with each class.
-Magic system is really fluid and allows you to feel like, a supportive mage, the effing powerful warlock that you want to be nuking everything in sight, a magic guarding and sword swinging mystic knight, or an extremely versatile battlefield controlling magic archer.
-Pawn system is easy to get into and you can make your pawn what you want to wether you want it to be a tank, healer, or even a sniping ranger, possibilities are fantastic but they can only choose from the basic or advanced classes and not the hybrids.
-Epic fights with tons of monsters in the main game and even more in the dark arisen Bitterblack Isle area.
-Dragons actually want to and will try to kill you rather than fly around and scream at you
-Different modes from the normal and hard modes to the speedrun modes.
-Game can use mods found on nexus
-Zombies are actually threatening
-Though no fast travel, as you play the game, you get port crystals that allow you to make your own fast travel points and you get the infinite ferrystone to use them.
-This game is both skill and stat based but you can play a balanced style and still do well in this game.
-Feels like playing an mmo without the elitests and Chinese gold farmers/sellers.
~Cons~
-The Guts and Griffith's (From the anime Berserk) armor are not in this game due to Capcom losing the rights to use them again.
-Story is not fantastic and is pretty much as bad as trying to fuse alot of fantasy anime stories together but everything else in this game more than makes up for it. If you watched Berserk you would even think you are doing an offbeat universe of the anime. There is even the princess gets your butt tortured in the dungeon scene.
-Pawns can be really dumb since pawn AI is really weird but it also results in funny moments but can result in frustrating ones as well like pawns jumping over chests and into death pits or deep water.
-Camera can be really annoying when it comes to climing large monsters especially animal based ones like a chimera causing you to climb and move around on them awkwardly.
All in all this is a great game. Capcom tried something and it worked really well. This game feels like everything everyone wants in an action rpg fantasy epic and with the combat, the atmosphere, monsters, classes, etc it all ties in really well with the play your way they did it. I would recommend this game to everyone.

I don't understand all the positive reviews.  Granted, I only wandered around for about an hour, but in that time I completed every item on the "beginner checklist", and then went on to make a base and hunt quite a few different enemies.
- The building system, crafting system, and the map are all complete rips from The Forest.  An exact copy.
- The art isn't great - it looks like old Unity 4 graphics, before Unity spent time working on PC shaders.
- The animations also aren't great - they look like they were bought from an asset store.
- The AI is incredibly simple and lifeless.  Every enemy in the game walks up to you, waits 2 seconds, then attacks.  It repeats until one of you die.
- The inventory system is painful to work with.
- There are no other features in the game that I can think of.  I crafted armor, weapons and food, I built structures, and I explored and killed enemies.
I'm not going to reference all the bugs and odd game design choices (like spawning an advanced weapon next to where I first spawned) since it's Early Access.  The graphics and the animations I can also get over since it's Early Access (though the developers behind this game aren't indie and won't improve either category before launch, I applaud them for taking advantage of this marketing tactic).
However, the outright stealing of not only the concept but the implementation of this game's core features (building, crafting, map) is appaling.  I don't see any way for this game to rise above the other 400 piles of crap that have hastily flooded the 'Survival' genre looking for easy money.
The first response to this might be "well you haven't tried playing online with others - that's where the fun is."  Why would I want to repeat what I just did with others?  It's still the same crap AI, stolen building and crafting systems, and empty, desolate environment where the fog is so heavy you can't see more than 20 meters in any direction?  Why does the developer need to rely on my wanting to kill another player (or build something with him) in order to have fun?  Bottom line, I'll go play ARK or Rust or The Forest or one of the other 400 Survival games that have done all these things much better.
Even though this is Early Access, no developer is going to fundamentally change all of their core features prior to "launch".  I expect almost no changes or additions to this game for a long, long time.

Another Perspective is a simple 2D platformer puzzle game where you control an unnamed protagonist and have to move from room to room by solving the puzzle contained in each room.
The puzzles are solved by looking at them from “another perspective”, some rooms contain multiple versions of yourself and when you switch between your different selves the room and how you can interact with it changes. The goal is to use each version of yourself in tandem to piece together the greater puzzle.
The game has a short, but lovey soundtrack, pleasant graphics, simple gameplay, and what I consider to be a rather unique plot, and of course above all, fun to solve puzzles. As a fan of the Portal series I was able to enjoy this game quite thoroughly.
However there are some downsides, the game is incredibly short and will probably take you about an hour to run through, two if you want to discover the “true” ending. There is even an achievement for making it through all the rooms in 12 minutes which should give you a good idea of how short this game is. I also experienced a slightly annoying graphics glitch where parts of the screen would flash in red, but it was not enough to stop me enjoying the game, though I would not recommend buying it at its full price, perhaps grab it on a special or in a bundle as I did.

This is an even better game than the Baldur's Gate series, and is almost as good at telling a story as Planescape: Torment. Kotaku had an article where it said: "You know you have a good game when you reroll after a few hours just to test another class". I rerolled, and I think I might just do another shortly to test the Cipher and/or Druid.
The story and writing sucks you in and holds you to it's bosom from the minute you start in the caravan camp. And unlike other games you are given clues to what is happening, but nothing else. Which gets your head going. And this part, in addition to the beautiful graphics is what makes it occupy far too much of my time (even when I turn it off).
Colorful NPCs with a story to tell makes the game even more engrossing. The same goes for the game world PoE is set in. It's something completely new and alot less black and white than you find in other games. Being the good guy isn't always the same thing as helping people by completing quests. Sure, some of the NPCs are pretty stereotypical, like the animancer early in the first act, but others are not so obvious. It makes it more fun. And because your choices in the dialogues have a direct impact on your own power (turn off the information on what choices give what reputation for extra fun) you really have to think your way through things.

I purchased Myworld mainly because I really, really like the team behind this. I've been using Gameguru since its launch - before that, I used FPS Creator too - , so when I found out that the craziest mind in the team - Ravey - was behind this project, I just needed to purchase it.
So, after I finished my work (about 6 a.m.) I decided I would give this a try. After making a run in two of the pre-made levels -which are really satisfying, in a weird way -, I went straight to the level editor, thinking about spending some 15 minutes on it before I went to bed. Two and a half hours later, and making a huuuuge effort, I managed to gather up the will to shutdown the program, asking myself what-happened-here.
Let me start by saying that the combat in Myworld looks quite similar to the one found in most new generation RPGs, following the formula of the Dark Souls series, and similar. It's pretty solid, and it works. Can't say much more about it however, as I really dislike DS and similar games - my combat needs to be fast, energetic and franctic - , yet I have faith in that the developers will add several alternatives to it, including different classes of heroes, which they have already confirmed. The environments look great, the art is absolutely original, and there's a whole lot of objects to place, break, place some more, and keep on breaking. There are also several kinds of enemies, each with their own characteristics, including creatures that can't be stunned, and even bosses, one of them a summoner; and a solid waypoint system reminiscent of that found in Gameguru (which I am thankful for).
The editor, well... it's just awesome. There are quite a lot of tools that allow to shape the terrain any way you want, making the ground possibilities almost infinite. A nice assortment of buildings, gates, adornments, and other neat stuff, in a collection of assets that will continue to grow, talking from experience here (Gameguru, remember?). There are some nice background picks out there, and here's hoping for a lot more. But I believe my favourite thing, one that I did not expect and made me spend countless minutes modifying things is... the paint tool. Yes indeed, you can paint your terrain any way you like. Green mountains with reddish stripes, colored with brown moats here and there? No problem! White ground, brown pathway and a surreal pink border crossing the town? Well, why not! A desertic landscape with violet and orange dunes? OF COURSE!!! I believe that is an amazing, incredibly versatile tool that will lead to a whole universe of creations from many different people. And boy, do I hope that they add it to Gameguru too... one can dream, right?
To close up: if you want to make lighter darksoul-ish quick levels, chain them to a whole game, and play them with your friends, family, neighbours and whoever you want, then this is the software for you. TGC has been working in the game creation industry for quite a while now. They have experience, they deliver, and they keep their promises, always listening to what the community has to say. Speaking of which, if this community gets to be half as good as Gameguru's one, it will be just awesome. I absolutely recommend this game, and can't wait to spend my breaks building levels, testing them, and sharing them.
Suggestions: 1- the quest editor needs two more things: conditions (needed to take this quest) and rewards. 2- a little more variety in friendly characters. We need a town marshall, a priest, a jailer... you know, the typical medieval types. 3- flying enemies would not be bad at all. 4- some sounds are a little stale, mainly the character's sword. Do you accept collaborations? 5- Modular buildings. Oh, yeah.
And finally, a message for Ravey... WHERE'S MAH JINGLE PACK???
Keep it up guys ;)

So Soccer Rage is a new early access title that combines soccer and a fighting game in one. Conceptually it sounds pretty great. However, after playing a few matches it just seems to fall short for me.
In a futuristic setting where soccer has become bloodsport you find Soccer Rage. Both sides start with 11 players plus a goalie and must either win the match or beat the opposing team into submission. Each player has a health bar and takes damage when then are tackled, shouldered, or through a minigame expressed through a Street Fighter styled fighting game.
On its face this seems great. The ability to not take any penalties and play a NFL Blitz styled soccer game is great. I love the idea. It just doesn't execute either side of the game particularly well.
You are dropped into the game and the only option is to play a quick match. I'm okay with this considering it's in early access. You then have to read controls because otherwise you won't know what to do. The controls for the soccer portion of the game are pretty straight forward. Pass, shoot, long pass, and through ball are all accounted for. There are also more involved controls like jumping, curving shots and the rage mechanic. I, however, could not figure out how to get any of the controls that used the Left Bumper or L1 buttons plus another button to work properly. I didn't feel like I could hold onto the ball long enough to actually execute any of these skills. Actually, I couldn't figure out what I was doing at all really. Everything felt sluggish to me. Passing seemed poor, switching characters was inaccurate, and shooting the ball was near impossible. The whole soccer portion seemed incomplete and just not fun to play.
Every once in awhile you'd get into a fight which dropped you into a 2D fighting game where you have no idea what buttons do what. I have to assume there's a light/heavy punch/kick but not sure which was which. There are also a few special moves which I button mashed my way to figuring out. However, much like the soccer portion, the fighting portion is slow, confusing and nonresponsive.
This game has so much promise though, the concept is there. A heavy action oriented sports game seems awesome on the surface. The futuristic gladiator style gameplay is nice. Though neither side of the coin is executed particularly well. The soccer side is no Fifa and the fighting side is no Street Fighter. So you're left with a game that's hard to control, with mediocre graphics and a great concept. It's unfortunate.
I think if the developer went in a more arcade route like the aforementioned NFL Blitz and went with a 5v5 game with simplified controls the game would be much better IMO. I'd love to play a 5v5 version online with all real players.
I'll wait and see what happens with Soccer Rage but for now I'd have to pass. I'm hoping to see this game find it's happy medium between sports sim and fighting game.

Like most people have said in previous reviews this game has a lot of potential to be a decent game. Just some aspects need changing and improving.
For example the game is really fast,  It's chaotic. It doesn't really allow for you to pass the ball, dribble past opponents or perform long passes. So I would like to see the gameplay slowed down so you can actually play the soccer side of the game.

I'm not sure if you can block because there is no move set at the moment so that makes it even harder.
Shooting could be slightly improved as I find that I can't aim my shots in to the corners. They always seem to go straight towards the goalkeeper.

What I do like is how you can literally destroy oppponents by just sliding in to them, shoulder smashing them and all round beating the living hell out of them ha. It feels satisfying when they break through about to shoot and you slide in behind and break them in half ha!
You either win the game by scoring most goals overall or by destroying opponents, rendering them useless and taking them down to 6 players  (I think it is 6 players) and then you have to foreit. Many times I've been 3-0 up but lost because they have owned me in all the fights and lost my players to death haha.
So as it stands at the moment it is quite basic with just the one game mode and simple (yet chaotic gameplay) and a very hard fighting mechanic in my opinion. I do believe that it could be a really good game if they just slowed the gameplay down, improved the fighting and improved the shooting.  I'm sure they will update the game throughout the next few weeks so maybe hang on til they do that and improve the game before you purchase. Either way I had fun playing the game and look forward to future updates.

Soccer Rage sounds like a fun game, a mixture between a fighting game and FIFA soccer that I played with.
While the game is in beta, I wanted to do a beta preview, not the actual review of the game in whole since it is not complete.  As it is Early Access, the game does have a great amount of potential.  Here are the following pros and cons:
Pros
-Soccer!  What more could you ask for?
-National teams for countries to play with
-Fighting implemented like in NHL where you must duke it out between both players.
-Unique animations in the fighting styles
-Unique uniforms for both Local and Away teams
Cons
-Early Access

Special notes for Game Developer:
Using the button to exit out of Replay and Kickoff results in both Replay and Kickoff text to appear at the same time.
When I enter into fight mode, the AI continues to fight me even if I am not prepared.  While executing my controls before the screen shows two players fighting, my player keeps on fighting without me knowing about it.  There's no proper executing of the fight scene before it begins.  Holding the AI and player from fighting until the words announced, "Fight!" ends should help.
The AI opposing team is too fast, and are capable of playing the ball against a newcomer to this game.  Slowing them down, or potentially beefing up the player 1's AI along with the goalie would help.  The goalie would not defend the post after a few rounds.  After my goalie entered into a Rage fight with someone and won, he refused to defend the post.  He would stand there and then receive hit after hit with the ball.  So amazing he can survive such encounters!
Whenever I switch to a new player on my team, I noticed that the previous player I selected stops.  It just stands there for a few seconds before rushing to move into its position.  If I select the one player repeatedly, the player can't move for a second or more.  It results in a loss of the ball, loss of movement, and unable to defend aggressively.
These are mostly some of the reasons why I lost my first Quickmatch as Germany against Japan!  0-8...  *shudders*...  Not ever doing that again.  :P  They're a World Cup winner in 2014!  Not World Cup losers, haha.

I think the community puts too much of an emphisis on the difficulty of this game, It's not that hard, you just need to know what your doing.
First off, they put a lot of work into this games lore, they really know how to build the world and make it feel real. (You do need to go looking for it though, read item descriptions)
The voice acting is iffy for some characters, and absolutly increadible for even more
The combat is amazing, it teaches you to balance dodges, blocks, parries, attacks, kicks, and healing. I've gotten sick of games where you just have to walk up to an enemy and press buttons to win. Dark Souls: Prepare to Die is a game of skill, not luck.
If you have friends who play this game, don't listen to them most of the time. A friend of mine told me I'd have such a hard time fighting the "Four Kings," and I beat it on my first try. The game is about intimidation, and it does a very good job at it, just use your brain to guide your hands, not your hands and nothing more.
There are several moments in the game where it becomes outrageously unfair, but the rest of the game outweighs such parts
You will die many, many times, but a lot of deaths does not point to impossibility or unfairness
This is a very polished game, and I recomend it to you 100%

An extremely fun and addictive game. Dont let its aesthetics fool you. It offers a win chance for all skill levels aswell. Even if you are terrible player like me still there are some runs where RNG  god shines on you and you become the destroyer of worlds. The feeling when you become unstoppable and clear rooms in single shot is indescribable.

So finally, after playing 707 hours of this and getting all 276 achievements, I think it's time to finally write a review for this game.
It's hard to discuss why this game is so addictive. Best to look up some professional game journalist's/critics analysis of the it (Yahtzee is a good one to start with, although he reviewed the original Isaac, no WOTL update or Rebirth/Afterbirth)
This game may seem too big to dive into, but rest assured, it's well worth it. Yes it's hard, but most of the time not stupidly hard. Ok, one or two of the characters are not fun to play with and there are a couple of challenges that are stupid difficult, but that sgould not deter you from getting it. If you never have played a Roguelike game before (like I had when I started this) this is a brilliant introduction. It's not stupidly Nintendo-hard, (like Spelunky) nor does it have a small amount of variety and customisation. Every game always feels like a fresh new playthrough, even some of the bad runs you will inevitably have.
Anyway, I'm waffling. If you're like me and are sometimes afraid of trying new things, than I highly suggest to get out of your comfort zone like I did and dive into the world of Isaac.
All the best everyone! :3

I absolutely loved this one.
Like a perfect blend between Bioshock and Half-Life in terms of gameplay, in a setting which kind of reminds of Metro 2033 with a story as twisting as Bioshock Infinte.
I heard of this game by mere coincidence, as some would say, or rather, echoes in the time-space; and decided to look it up. It is true as many people say, this is a game which has not really gotten the attention it deserves. Maybe a little overshadowed by the titles mentioned above. But anyone who enjoyed those games will love this one, as it is a awesome hybrid between them all.
It also kind of takes you back (intended) to a time when gaming was simple yet satisfying. Not extremely complex mechanics and character leveling and ability systems. There are some character and equipment upgrades which can be done, and although they affect the gameplay a lot, it does not really take the attention away from the game.
Secrets and bonuses are not that challenging to find, yet rewarding. And there are some really neat references, both subtle and blatantly obvious.
You will most likely experience at least one 'jump scare' and one annoying puzzle mechanic. But other than that, it is more a 'aim, shoot, kill and reload' kind of game with a really intriguing story with several endings.
Some parts of the story are actually possible to foresee and calculate beforehand, but the twists and time theory will get your mind blown at least once.
Needlessly to say, it is a game well worth your attention and money. The game is of a satisfying length with all the classic elements and phases and will not consume too much of your time... he. he.
I loved the ending which I experienced, with the subtle hints embedded.
There are a major amount of red lines (or stars) to build upon, if one would ever find time to explain.

Singularity is often overlooked because it didn't do so well when it was released back in 2010, which is a bit of a shame because this is a solid shooter with a pretty nice story, satisfying combat and a cool time shifting gameplay mechanic. It's also not hard to see that the game is heavily influenced by Half-Life 2.
The graphics hold up well despite it's age and it runs smooth as butter without issues on modern systems like Windows 10. FOV is a bit of a problem though, being way too small, some people might experience motion sickness because of this. Luckily there are programs like Flawless Widescreen that will fix this easily without any tampering with the game files.
The game is a little short though, it will take you about 7 to 8 hours to finish it and the ending is a bit lackluster. That said, this is Raven Software's last game before being swallowed up by Activision and being the developers of such classics as Hexen, Soldier of Fortune, the Star Wars Jedi Knight series and Wolfenstein, you know they can provide an action packed game and that's exactly what Singularity is, short but sweet, and well worth a purchase for any FPS fan.

Now, the CONs:

This is advertised as a game development engine for action rpg enthusiast.  Sounds great!  The only thing this engine has going for it is the ease of use.  When I purchase an engine to make my own creations (as advertised on the website), I should be allowed to decide the balancing. Things like weapon strength and game balancing are all decided for you?  Wait though, isn't that up to me?  The creator?  Nope, not here. The engines developer does that for you.  Wait, what? =D
However, as new updates come out, you are stuck with the engine developers stats and balancing they chose to offer you.
From a recent update we recieved:
* Weapon damage balancing
* Blue weapons of the next difficulty level will be better than previous level epics
* An epic weapon from one difficulty level is a good starting point for the next difficulty level
* Enemies in later difficulty levels no longer take seemingly endless hits to kill
* Spelling mistakes fixed in loot
* Healing over time and life on hit have been nerfed

* When you loot a weapon the info box showing what you received now comes up in the bottom left corner
* Elite boss now drops rare+ loot in line with the other bosses

* Increased the drop rate for legendary items
The only three positives I can honestly give this engine is the cheap price and the fact it has many assets to populate your "creations" with.  It is updated regularly.  However, it's advertised as an action rpg maker.  So when I seen this, I thought I was going to be given the opportunity to decide it's questing, looting, stats, etc.  My first thought was, "finally an rpg maker type engine, only in 3D!!"  I don't understand why these stats are chosen for me?  It's as if Unity3D was to come out and say "here create a first person shooter, but weapon strength and character run speed and health will be decided by us, not you the creator."

It's advertised as an customizable game engine for action rpg makers.  This is why I gave this engine a negative review.  My review honestly when I initially wrote it was positive, and now I'm changing that.  If it wasn't for the cheap price I would of asked for my money back.  I know and yes I do realize it's early access and things can change daily.  However, a big selling point for me was the ability to kind of run free with an engine like this, and I feel as though it does way to much hand holding.  This could honestly be the thing that takes a 2D Rpg Maker off the map, because the potential and developer are passionate about this project.  As of right now though, my review has to change.  I feel as though we are going to get nothing but cookie cutter projects that all feel, look and loot the same, just like when First Person Shooter Creator was first introduced to us in early 2000's.  However, at least you could customize in that engine.

I wrote a review previously, but after extensively using the editor to make my first map (It's called "Valdronaire", you should check it out!) I've decided to re-write it.
MyWorld is an RPG game as well as an RPG game maker. More specificially, the entire game runs on worlds. A world is basically one RPG map. That can be something you have made, something someone else has made, or one of the default maps that come installed with the game. Complete with an editor, MyWorld allows you to use the cute art style and already perfected physics and 3d mechanics to create your own map from scratch extremely easily! Now that you have a basis, lets dive into the pros and the cons of this game so far.
PROS:
~~~~~
*Great art style
*Outstanding potential (I don't even think a sham wow could handle all the potential this game is soaking in)
*Devs seem to be very passionate about the game
*HubWorld (HubWorld is the game's main menu screen basically, but instead of an actual screen, its an interactive world you can move around in, get used to the controls, etc. Very, very cool)
*Easy and accessible editor (Holy moly don't even get me started on this, the editor is absolutely amazing. It's user friendly, quick and easy (with the exception of a few cons listed below), and when you get the hang of it, it can yield amazing results in mere hours of work)
*Steam workshop accessibility (Don't know how to upload to the workshop but still want your exciting map available to your peers? No worries! The game takes care of that for you. With one easy click of a button the map you want is immediatley uploaded to the workshop for all to see.)
CONS:
~~~~~
Disclaimer*** MyWorld is in very early access, most of these cons will be fixed witht time.
*Lack of a player base (unless you're playing with friends, I have yet to find a multiplayer match)
*Lack of content (This especially shows in the editor, more specifically, the NPC section of the editor. It's very plain and extremely basic. There are no advanced options that I can find for NPCs besides creating an extremely basic quest. There could also be more placeable objects. Of course, this is something that I feel will continually be improved so I wouldn't fret)
So, overall, you're getting a load of pros in exchange for two cons that will get better with time. This game is extremely innovative, as well as exciting and fun to play and build with. I would recommend it to anyone looking for something new to spice up their account. Happy map making!

I got this game a few years ago. Back then it was still in beta, and while it had a fair amount of content, the story was lacking, the building felt empy, your ships were static, there were severe performance issues, and the balancing of weapons and abilities needed a lot of work.
I played it for a while, then set it down, because it was fun, but had limited merit.
When 1.0 came out recently, I decided to pick it up again and see what had changed.
Wow!
They really improved it. The game has a reasonably compelling story now, it has endless quests that are actually well implemented, you can build new villages, recruit new settlers, recruit more crew members to your ship and upgrade your ships from dinky boxes to hulking behemoths.
They've rebalanced things a lot, added more content, made farming awesome, and just created enough richness that you can enjoy the game for hundreds of hours.
When you've got max level gear, you can stomp the easy enemies, but you can still get killed by the strongest ones if you're reckless. The bosses are all dynamic and fun to fight, and this missions they added to get to them are frankly kind of awesome.
They've improved the richness of the cultures, even though they did have to remove a few things that didn't fit with the improved lore.
There are still things they could do to build upon the game and make it even better, but it's a fully functional version with a lot of cool features.
Some people compare the game to Terraria. I've played both, and here's what I'll say. Terraria's progression system is longer, there are a lot more steps, a lot more boss fights, and while you're doing that, Terraria might be more intense. However, once you've beaten the bosses a few times and maxed out your gear in Terraria, things just feel kind of empty. There's not enough end game content to keep you entertained for that long.
Starbound is different. There are a lot more biomes, sub-biomes, places to explore, and total content. Starbound has dozens of times the number of building items, and trillions of times the landmass to explore. There are so many cool little things that you'll discover on adventures that will make you smile, and the capacity to have pets, and to build new villages has really given you a reason to build cool places.
The developers have done a great job with this, and I hope they add even more cool things in the future. For $15, this is a great deal. Happy travels to you.

I first heard about this game roughly six years ago when I was first getting into FPS games. It was described to me as some sort of mashup of Half-Life and Metro. I looked up some videos and chalked it down as some generic activision broshooter.
I was wrong.
I don't really remember how this game ended up in my library. I think I'd last played it sometime in... 2013 or 2014? All I knew is I ended up liking it. I was scrolling through my library reorganizing all my games earlier today when I saw this game on the list and I thought to myself "somehow I don't remember anything about this game other than it being cool".
I'm a couple hours into my second playthrough and yes, this game is as cool as I remember. I think if you want to more accurately describe it compared to other games, it's Half-Life meets Metro with a sprinkle of Bioshock and RE5/6. All in a good way. At it's core it's something of an action horror game. It's got a few jumpscares and the voice acting is hit and miss, but the level design, though linear, is well-paced and entertaining and the setpieces are beautiful. Just remember. Train boss. Remember. It's a good setpiece.
Visually... It's a bit dated for a game released in 2010, considering it's an Xbox 360 port, but on a technical level, despite the lack of very advanced graphics settings, the game looks clean and crisp and it's not hard to look at. (I've picked a few screenshot-worthy scenes already.) Optimization is fine, can't say a lot on that front.
All in all, I think this game has sooorta fallen out of the spotlight and just like me, I don't think a lot of people even remember it exists. Definitely a hidden gem at this point. Pick it up.

The terrible port aside, Dark Souls is an action RPG with a heavy emphasis on patience and actual RPG elements. You roleplay a character of your own making, choosing his/her’s class, homeland, and starting gift. You’re promptly given a brief cutscene which really doesn’t tell you anything, then you’re on your own.
You find yourself in Firelink Shrine, a desolate yet homey location to call your camp. This is where you will spend most of your time talking to NPCs or purchasing equipment from merchants. Your newfound camp resides in the land of Lordran, a grim, depressing, and often times creepy environment. The characters follow suit, very few seem trustworthy, and even fewer seem genuine when talking with you, and all of them will regularly end their conversations with an unpleasant psychotic laugh. What you’re doing in Lordran, and where you’re supposed to be going isn’t clear, as the residents of this world try to help or hinder your adventure. It feels like the land is going through some kind of apocalypse, as hollowed-out humans and creatures wander about, prepared to mawl, crush or stab you on sight.
When it comes time to fight the hollows of Lordran, you’ll find the combat is rather slow and simulates real weight to your weaponry and armor, heavily punishing you when you try to rush or run past enemies. In most cases you’ll be standing in front of an enemy with your shield up, waiting for an opportunity to finally strike. This sets the pace for Dark Souls, being slow, meticulous, thoughtful and careful will often times bring the best rewards. This doesn’t just go for the combat either, if you’re aware of your surroundings you can often times see an ambush or trap ahead, which would otherwise feel unforgiving and difficult.
The story to Dark Souls isn’t very obvious, and much like the rest of the gameplay requires you to be thoughtful and aware to actually notice most of the stories being told. If you don’t have the patience for lore presented in a non-direct fashion, ignoring the overall story won’t really hamper your enjoyment either, as the lore of the world and characters are really just icing on the mechanics already there. If you’re interested in the lore, but like it being told in a more direct way, there are a plethora of quality videos online which showcase the story and lore.
You’ll see a lot of people saying “Dark Souls doesn’t hold your hand, and it will kick your♥♥♥♥♥” and that’s largely correct. You will be dropped in this large, relatively open area and unless if you pay very close attention to characters dialogue or contextual hints, you’ll be very lost. That’s precisely the experience you’re getting into when you play Dark Souls. If you go into this game with patience, wanderlust for a grim and sad world, the acceptance that you’ll probably die a lot, you will enjoy your time with Dark Souls much more.
Dark Souls captivated me back in 2012, and has since remained one of my favorite games. Although the PC port was terrible, the DSfix makes it bearable and the experience is worth the trouble in my opinion. If you haven’t already jumped into the series, Dark Souls Prepare to Die Edition goes on sale pretty regularly, and I highly recommend the game if anything I’ve said sounds enticing. Just remember, take it slow, be patient... and be prepared to die.

The Mass Effect series is one of my all-time favorites, followed closely by the Witcher. I have played at least 6 campaigns since I first bought the game several years ago.
Mass Effect is one of the best story- and choice-driven RPG games I've played since Baldur's Gate. It's a space opera with an incredible plot and amazing choice mechanics--your decisions matter in the long term and will determine both the consequences of this game and of Mass Effect 2 and 3--and it has aged very well as a result.
Character development is, in my opinion, second-to-none. The NPCs in your crew--and even some who aren't in your crew--have interesting relationships with Shepard, interesting backstories, and (despite the letdown of the Mass Effect 3 ending) fantastic character arc conclusions, which are even better if you get Mass Effect 3's Citadel DLC. The game universe is enormous and complex, and the story really gives you a good sense of how large it is as you fight your way through planets to complete missions.
There are three downsides:
1) The combat mechanics are rather boring. It's a third-person shooter that uses cover mechanics and not much else. You don't have ammo problems--your weapons will  just overheat (which changes for the better, in my opinion, in the second game). You can't dodge and it's generally unwise to charge at the enemy on the higher difficulties, regardless of your character class, so you really just end up feeling like a massive brick wall with a gun. If you're going to attempt insanity, it's almost not worth it to play anything but the soldier class because it synergizes best with the game mechanics and can naturally regenerate health.
However, I think the issues with the combat mechanics are more than compensated for by the quality of the story.
2) On a related note, the insanity difficulty is hard, but for bad reasons. It basically just amps up the health that enemies have by a lot and their damage by a little, making most battles drawn-out wars of attrition. If you're new, which I can't imagine is likely at this point, or coming from ME 2/3, I'd suggest you just play it on easy. Nobody's going to judge you. The point of the game is its storyline, in any case, and easy/normal are best for experiencing it without becoming frustated by large numbers of drawn-out battles.
3) After ME1, the combat mechanics improve exponentially, but the quality of the storyline declines. Compared to ME1, ME2 and 3 feel somewhat cheap. They're still worth it, and their stories are not by any means bad, but they are outshone by ME1 by quite a lot. The ending of the third game, particularly--even after the free DLC that EA put out to try to fix its problems--*will* leave you feeling cheated. The Citadel DLC will soften the blow considerably, though, so you should definitely get it, at the least. Aside from the beginning and ending of ME3, the storyline is solid and the major secondary plot points opened in ME1 and 2 are actually resolved very well.

A free mod, if you have a Source Engine running game, like Hl2, CSS etc.
Thanks to Half-life 1, Zombie Panic was spawned and thus after Hl2, a source engine running ZP was made as you see here.
Mainly really only a multiplayer game, players start out having to survive or escape the map, following objectives.
Soon after round start a random player will be picked to become a "special" zombie, one that has a larger chance of infecting players. When a player dies, they become a zombie themselves and must help kill out the rest of the surviving players.
Around the map you can find different sorts of weapons, ranging from melee to long/close range based weapons. The game also uses a ammo system, which you can decide what kind of ammo type and how much you want to drop. You see, the more you carry, the more burden you get, and become slower. You become a easy target for a swarm of zombies.
Items also include health packs, pills, body armor and wooden planks you can use to board against windows or doors to keep out zombies for a small amount of time.
The mod has a thriving community with a decent amount of servers, and there's loads of custom maps incase you become bored of the usual classic maps.
Overall I would highly recommend this mod if you enjoy zombie games.

If you’re a fan of third person action games, you’ll derive a lot of pleasure from this game. Responsive controls, simple but depth-filled combat, and a multitude of ways to change up your playstyle. Those who are looking for a slightly longer experience won’t find much to offer though. Despite the new game plus, a variety of customisable weapons, passive buffs in the form of ‘liquors’ and branching paths in the story, it lacks the depth and longevity of other titles such as Bayonetta and Devil May Cry, but it doesn’t require it. From the beautiful art style, to the enchanting world and lore, all topped off with a narrator akin to the likes of a dystopian Morgan Freeman, the game had me hooked. If that isn’t enough, then a beautifully weaved narrative that changes per your actions should be. Like a microcosmic Stanley Parable, minor actions can trigger the narrator to react to your behaviour accordingly. All this culminates into an experience that never seeks to do more than it can master, but what’s there is the benchmark of its genre.
Bastion is wonderfully charming and all consuming; well worth the time of any player.
